items.title: Stepwise intracoronary imaging assessment of lumen and vessel changes during drug-coated balloon angioplasty for in-stent restenosis.
items.abstract: Drug-coated balloon (DCB) angioplasty is an established treatment for in-stent restenosis (ISR), and its procedural success mainly depends on optimal lesion preparation. Angiography alone offers limited assessment of acute procedural effects, and sequential vessel and lumen changes have not been comprehensively characterized with intracoronary imaging (ICI). Therefore, we aimed to characterize the stepwise vessel and lumen changes during DCB angioplasty for ISR across three procedural stages: pre-lesion preparation, post-lesion preparation and post-DCB inflation. We retrospectively enrolled 20 patients (21 lesions) undergoing DCB angioplasty for ISR with available ICI pullbacks (intravascular ultrasound (IVUS), n = 16; optical coherence tomography (OCT), n = 5) at three stages: pre-lesion preparation, post-lesion preparation, and post-DCB inflation. Lesions treated with DCBs were identified on angiography and co-registered to the ICI pullbacks. Median age was 69 years, 15 patients (75%) were male, and lesion preparation was performed with non-compliant balloons in 76%. On IVUS, minimal lumen area (MLA) increased from 2.7 [2.2-3.5]mm 2 at baseline to 4.8 [4.1-6.0]mm 2 after lesion preparation (median difference (95% confidence interval) +2.6 (1.8-2.7)mm 2 , p  2 post-DCB (+0.6 (0.4-1.1)mm 2 , p  2 at baseline to 3.8 [2.9-4.2]mm 2 after lesion preparation (+2.0 [0.3-2.8]mm 2 ), and 4.5 [3.9-5.3]mm 2 post-DCB (+0.6 [0.3-1.0]mm 2 ). Neointimal burden decreased after lesion preparation and decreased further after DCB treatment. ICI demonstrates that the principal morphologic changes are achieved after lesion preparation, with smaller yet significant additional acute mechanical effects following DCB treatment.

items.title: γ-Glutamyl Transferase as a Practical Predictor of Elevated Liver Stiffness in Heart Failure　- Findings From a Daily Clinical Setting.
items.abstract: Liver stiffness assessed by liver elastography has been reported as useful for predicting hepatic congestion and outcomes in patients with heart failure (HF). However, liver elastography is not widely available for patients with HF in routine clinical settings. We investigated whether simple biomarkers can predict elevation of liver stiffness. In all, 52 hospitalized patients with HF were recruited to this study. The primary analysis examined the association between γ-glutamyl transferase (GGT) and liver stiffness in the overall study population. In multivariable linear regression analysis adjusted for age and sex, log-transformed GGT was independently associated with liver stiffness. This association remained significant in separate sensitivity analyses incorporating systolic and diastolic blood pressure, estimated glomerular filtration rate, N-terminal pro B-type natriuretic peptide, ejection fraction, tricuspid regurgitation pressure gradient, inferior vena cava diameter, inferior vena cava collapsibility index, and sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor use. In exploratory analyses for the prediction of high liver stiffness (>7.1 kPa), the addition of GGT increased integrated discrimination improvement and improved the net reclassification index, whereas the change in the area under the curve was not statistically significant. Direct comparison between models including GGT and the Fibrosis-4 index did not show a significant difference. GGT levels may provide a simple and clinically accessible signal associated with elevated liver stiffness in patients with HF and possible hepatic congestion.

items.title: Prevalence of Atrial Cardiopathy Biomarkers Across Ischemic Stroke Subtypes.
items.abstract: Atrial cardiopathy (AC) has been proposed as a potential embolic mechanism in embolic stroke of undetermined source (ESUS); however, the distribution of AC biomarkers across ischemic stroke subtypes remains unclear. We retrospectively analyzed 533 consecutive patients with acute ischemic stroke. Stroke subtypes were classified as small-vessel occlusion (SVO), branch atheromatous disease (BAD), large-artery atherosclerosis (LAA), ESUS, or cardioembolism (CE). AC was defined according to ARCADIA trial criteria as the presence of at least one of the following: P-wave terminal force in lead V1 (PTFV1) >5,000 μV·ms, N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) >250 pg/mL, or left atrial diameter index (LADI) ≥3 cm/m 2 . We evaluated the prevalence and overlap of these biomarkers across subtypes. AC biomarkers were significantly more frequent in CE than in other subtypes. Using ≥1 biomarker, AC prevalence was 43% in SVO, 49% in BAD, 53% in LAA, 54% in ESUS, and 97% in CE. With ≥2 biomarkers, prevalence decreased to 8%, 7%, 13%, 19%, and 78%, respectively. NT-proBNP elevation was the most common biomarker across all groups. Left atrial enlargement was rare in non-CE subtypes (~5%) and showed no overlap with PTFV1 in SVO, BAD, or LAA. While AC defined by ARCADIA criteria is highly prevalent in CE, it is also widely observed across other stroke subtypes. Refinement of AC definitions, including stricter thresholds and/or biomarker combinations, may better identify atrial dysfunction with causal relevance to stroke.

items.title: Underlying Plaque Type and Neoatherosclerosis After ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction　- Serial Optical Coherence Tomography Substudy of the CONNECT Trial.
items.abstract: The relationship between underlying plaque type and the development of neoatherosclerosis remains uncertain. This was a secondary analysis of the CONNECT trial, which randomized 239 patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) to receive biodegradable polymer or durable polymer everolimus-eluting stents. Patients with serial optical coherence tomography (OCT) were included and post-procedural OCT frames that corresponded to segments showing neoatherosclerosis at the 3-year follow-up (NA-leading segments) were identified by manual frame matching. At the frame level, we compared post-procedural OCT findings in NALS to 2 comparators: non-NA-leading lesions (lesions without neoatherosclerosis); and non-NA-leading segments within NA-leading lesions. Of 144 lesions with serial OCT, neoatherosclerosis occurred in 17 (11.8%). In NA-leading segments, compared to non-NA-leading lesions and non-NA-leading segments within NA-leading lesions, the proportion of frames with lipid-rich plaque was higher (71% vs. 54% [odds ratio (OR) 2.72; 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.23-6.01] and 58% [OR 2.62; 95% CI 0.99-6.96], respectively). Similarly, the mean (±SD) in-stent atherothrombotic material area was larger in NA-leading segments (0.41±0.39 vs. 0.24±0.31 [geometric mean ratio (GMR) 2.00; 95% CI 1.21-3.29] and 0.16±0.16 mm 2 [GMR 2.33; 95% CI 1.26-4.31], respectively). Underlying lipid-rich plaque and a higher burden of in-stent atherothrombotic material were associated with neoatherosclerosis at 3 years in STEMI patients, indicating that plaque composition at the time of DES implantation may critically influence neoatherosclerosis formation.

items.title: Trough Rivaroxaban Plasma Concentrations and Early Thrombus Regression in Acute Pulmonary Embolism: A Sub-analysis of the SAKURA-PE/DVT REGISTRY.
items.abstract: Objectives　To evaluate the association between trough rivaroxaban plasma concentrations and early thrombus regression in patients with acute pulmonary embolism (PE).Methods　This study was a sub-analysis of the multicenter, prospective SAKURA PE/DVT REGISTRY. The thrombus regression rate was calculated using contrast-enhanced computed tomography performed at diagnosis and approximately two weeks after treatment initiation. Trough rivaroxaban plasma concentrations were measured using a chromogenic anti-factor Xa assay. Correlations between plasma concentrations, thrombus regression rates, and coagulation parameters were analyzed.Patients　Among 153 patients with acute PE treated with direct oral anticoagulants, 106 received rivaroxaban, and trough plasma concentrations were measured in 51 patients.Results　The median trough rivaroxaban plasma concentration was 120.0 (55.6-186.0) ng/mL, with substantial interindividual variability. Trough rivaroxaban plasma concentrations were positively correlated with the thrombus regression rate in all patients (ρ = 0.33, P = 0.018) and in the intensive therapy group (ρ = 0.41, P = 0.009). In the multivariable analysis, log-transformed rivaroxaban plasma concentrations were independently associated with the thrombus regression rate in the intensive therapy group (β = 9.79, 95% confidence interval 0.72-18.86; P = 0.035). Prothrombin time was strongly correlated with rivaroxaban plasma concentration (ρ = 0.85, P < 0.001). Plasma concentrations tended to increase with age and showed greater variability in elderly patients.Conclusion　Higher trough rivaroxaban plasma concentrations were associated with greater early thrombus regression in patients with acute PE. Prothrombin time may be a practical surrogate for rivaroxaban exposure and may support individualized anticoagulation strategies in selected patients.

items.title: The Place of Therapeutic Apheresis in Severe Immune-Related Adverse Events: A Scoping Review of Literature.
items.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have revolutionized the management of patients with cancer. However, they can induce breakdowns in immunologic tolerance, leading to autoimmune diseases, or immune related adverse events (irAEs). These irAEs can sometimes be life threatening, requiring aggressive management, such as immunosuppressant (IS) or even therapeutic apheresis (TA). TA, an extracorporeal circulation technique, may represent a therapeutic option for severe irAEs, reducing their severity and duration by removing ICIs, pathogenic antibodies or inflammatory cytokines, although its role in this situation remains underreported. We made scoping review to better identify the use of TA for managing severe irAEs. From January 2022 to August 2025, three databases were reviewed, for articles mentioning the use of TA in the event of immunotoxicity. Only case reports or case series were retained. A descriptive summary was produced in table forms. Between 2022 and 2025, 162 articles were identified, 34 articles concerning 42 patients treated for severe irAE via TA were included. The underlying cancers were mainly non-small cell lung cancer and melanoma, and 78% of patients were treated with monotherapy anti-PD(L)1. The main indications for TA were neurological (40.6%), overlap manifestations (23.8%), and hepatitis (21.4%), mainly highly severe. TA was most often used in rescue situations, that is, after failure of several lines of IS. Complications of TA were rare. Clinical improvement was reported in most patients, usually within days of TA, with 24% complete resolution, and 45% partial resolution. Despite revolutionizing cancer treatment, ICIs induce severe irAEs, with poorly defined therapeutic options. TA may be a therapeutic option for life threatening irAEs, with data in the literature assuming its effectiveness. However, details on its use remain poorly defined. Further studies are required to emphasize its use as in irAEs.

items.title: [Natural killer cells: from basic discovery toward translational insights].
items.abstract: Natural killer (NK) cells are cytotoxic lymphocytes that play an essential role in controlling viral infections and cancer. Although tumor cells and virus-infected cells with reduced expression of major histocompatibility complex (MHC) class I molecules can escape from T cell-mediated immune responses, NK cells use a variety of receptors to recognize and efficiently eradicate these targets through cytotoxic activity. NK cells are also an attractive tool for the development of therapies for incurable viral infections and cancer. However, effective strategies to enhance NK cell-mediated immune responses have not yet been established. This article provides an overview of the mechanisms underlying target recognition by NK cells. It also explains the adaptive immune features, including antigen-specific proliferation and differentiation into memory NK cells, as an emerging aspect of NK cell biology. Furthermore, it outlines chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) NK cell therapy as a therapeutic approach for invigorating the anti-tumor activity of NK cells, and reviews recent research trends, including the current status and challenges of CAR-NK cells.

items.title: [CAR-T cell therapy for systemic autoimmune rheumatic diseases: a new frontier in immune reset therapy].
items.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor T (CAR-T) cell therapy, originally established for hematologic malignancies, has recently attracted attention as a novel therapeutic strategy for systemic autoimmune rheumatic diseases. By targeting CD19, CAR-T cells induce broad depletion of autoreactive B cells, leading to immune reconstitution. In systemic autoimmune rheumatic diseases, B cells play a central role not only in autoantibody production but also in antigen presentation and cytokine-mediated immune responses. Therefore, comprehensive elimination of B cells is considered an effective approach for disease control. Early clinical studies have demonstrated high remission rates in refractory cases, including systemic lupus erythematosus, with some patients achieving drug-free remission, suggesting deeper disease control beyond that attainable with conventional therapies. In terms of safety, cytokine release syndrome and neurotoxicity are generally milder than those observed in hematologic malignancies. In addition, a characteristic toxicity known as local immune effector cell-associated toxicity syndrome (LICATS) has been reported, presenting as transient inflammation localized to previously affected organs. Future challenges include optimizing CAR-T cell design with an emphasis on safety and controllability, as well as determining the optimal timing of treatment. CAR-T cell therapy holds curative potential and may redefine the treatment paradigm for systemic autoimmune rheumatic diseases.

items.title: [Third-party virus-specific T-cell therapy for treatment-resistant viral infections after hematopoietic cell transplantation].
items.abstract: Hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT) is a potentially curative treatment for severe disorders, including refractory hematologic malignancies and inborn errors of immunity. The increasing use of HLA-haploidentical transplantation and intensive immunosuppressive strategies has resulted in a growing population of patients at high risk for post-transplant viral infections. Viral infections after HCT are often refractory to currently available antiviral agents and remain a major cause of transplant-related morbidity and mortality. Effective viral control requires the reconstitution of virus-specific immunity; however, donor-derived antiviral immune responses often take considerable time to develop after transplantation. Against this background, virus-specific T-cell (VST) therapy has emerged as a promising immunotherapeutic approach. Recent advances have led to the development of third-party (TP), off-the-shelf VST products and multi-virus-specific T-cell (MVST) products capable of targeting multiple viruses simultaneously. Cryopreserved VST products enable rapid therapeutic intervention for patients with refractory viral infections. Furthermore, the approval of tabelecleucel for Epstein-Barr virus-associated post-transplant lymphoproliferative disease in Europe marks an important milestone in the clinical translation of VST therapy. This review summarizes the history, manufacturing strategies, clinical development, and key clinical trial results of VST therapy, with a particular focus on TP-VST and TP-MVST platforms and their development in Japan.

items.title: [T-cell redirecting therapies for multiple myeloma: an update].
items.abstract: T-cell redirecting therapies, particularly BCMA-directed CAR-T-cell therapy and bispecific antibodies, have substantially advanced the treatment of multiple myeloma. These therapies induce deep responses in patients with relapsed or refractory disease after exposure to proteasome inhibitors, immunomodulatory drugs, and anti-CD38 antibodies, and are increasingly being used in earlier lines of therapy. However, the availability of multiple BCMA-targeted approaches, including CAR-T-cell therapy, bispecific antibodies, and belantamab mafodotin, has made treatment selection increasingly complex. In clinical practice, it is important to consider not only efficacy, but also treatment sequence, bridging therapy before CAR-T-cell infusion, effects on subsequent therapies, treatment access, and patient-specific risks. In addition, GPRC5D-targeted therapy and dual-target strategies may provide new options for patients previously treated with BCMA-targeted therapies and for those with extramedullary disease. Long-term management, including infection prevention, hypogammaglobulinemia, prolonged cytopenias, and secondary malignancies, is also becoming increasingly important. This review summarizes the current clinical role of T-cell redirecting therapies in relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma, with a focus on treatment sequencing, extramedullary disease, long-term management, and future directions.

items.title: Dual-mode cross-validating biosensor based on a biomimetic Molecular Burr probe for quantitative autoimmune disease evaluation.
items.abstract: Antinuclear antibodies (ANA) serve as important serological biomarkers for autoimmune disease evaluation. However, existing detection methods rely predominantly on qualitative or semi-quantitative readouts that are susceptible to subjective interpretation. Herein, we report a quantitative dual-mode cross-validating biosensor for ANA detection based on a biomimetic Molecular Burr (MoB) probe. Constructed on an intrinsically fluorescent covalent organic framework (COF) scaffold, the MoB probe features a burr-like multivalent surface for antibody immobilization. Through systematic stepwise optimization, the probe achieved an antibody immobilization efficiency of 94.01%, together with fluorescence and peroxidase-mimicking catalytic activity within a single nanoarchitecture. By integrating intrinsic COF fluorescence and the peroxidase-mimicking activity of COF-supported platinum nanoparticles, the biosensor generated independent fluorescent and colorimetric outputs for mutual cross-validation. Under optimized conditions, the biosensor achieved a detection limit of 271 pg/mL across a linear range of 0.1-2000 ng/mL. Validation using 160 clinical serum samples demonstrated high concordance with a commercial enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. In a dedicated cohort of patients with autoimmune hepatitis and healthy controls, quantitative ANA was combined with alanine aminotransferase, aspartate aminotransferase, and immunoglobulin G. The resulting model yielded an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.967. This work establishes a sensitive, objective, and quantitative platform for ANA detection through complementary optical readouts. The results further support the potential value of quantitative ANA as a component of multiparametric assessment for autoimmune hepatitis.

items.title: The present and future of HIV and viral hepatitis co-infection.
items.abstract: HIV and hepatitis virus co-infection remains a major global health challenge, driven by shared transmission routes, populations with overlapping modes of acquisition, and potentially compounded disease progression. Co-infections of HIV and hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis C virus (HCV) remain prevalent, particularly among people who live in endemic areas, key populations, people who inject drugs, men who have sex with men, and migrants from endemic regions. Antiretroviral therapy is shifting towards regimens without HBV activity, increasing the risk for HBV infection or reactivation in some individuals. Although direct-acting antivirals have reduced active HCV infection considerably in many high-income settings, residual disease burden, reinfections, and inequitable access to treatment persist. Hepatitis delta virus continues to represent a severe but underdiagnosed co-infection among individuals with HIV-HBV co-infection, with insufficient global surveillance data. Acute hepatitis A and E increasingly affect people with HIV, presenting both as outbreak-related and sporadic cases, particularly in the context of suboptimal vaccination coverage. Contemporary management emphasises systematic screening, vaccination, integrated antiviral strategies, and public health interventions to reduce liver-related morbidity and mortality in people with HIV.

items.title: Estrogen Use and Porphyria Cutanea Tarda.
items.abstract: Estrogen-containing therapy is considered a risk factor for porphyria cutanea tarda (PCT), but the evidence is limited to clinical series and case reports. To investigate whether estrogen-containing therapy is associated with incident PCT, overall and according to estrogen-containing therapy type and route of administration. In this matched case-control study using data from Danish nationwide registries conducted from January 1, 1995, through November 1, 2024, female individuals with a first-time hospital diagnosis of PCT were matched 1:100 with population control patients on age, sex, and index date. At least 1 redeemed prescription of estrogen-containing therapy within 1 year before the index date. Odds ratios (ORs) with 95% CIs for incident PCT were calculated from conditional logistic regression. Analyses were stratified by estrogen-containing therapy type and route of administration. Analyses were adjusted for PCT-related comorbidities: HIV infection; liver disease, viral hepatitis, or iron overload; smoking-related diagnosis or treatment; and alcohol or drug misuse diagnosis or treatment. The study included 438 female case patients with incident PCT (median age, 61.16 years [IQR, 51.08-69.17 years]) and 43 800 age-matched female control patients. In total, 154 cases (35.16%) and 9433 control patients (21.54%) had been exposed to any estrogen-containing therapy within 1 year before the index date (adjusted OR, 2.03; 95% CI, 1.66-2.49). Estrogen-containing contraceptives were associated with incident PCT (adjusted OR, 2.52; 95% CI, 1.67-3.82) as were estrogen-only therapy (adjusted OR, 1.58; 95% CI, 1.23-2.03), and combined estrogen and progestogen therapy (adjusted OR, 2.18; 95% CI, 1.53-3.11). When stratified by route of administration, oral therapy was associated with PCT (adjusted OR, 2.44; 95% CI, 1.66-3.59), whereas nonoral routes were not. This nationwide matched case-control study found that estrogen-containing therapy was associated with incident PCT. In route-specific analyses, only oral therapy was associated with PCT, suggesting that route of administration should be considered when evaluating estrogen exposure as a potential risk factor for PCT.

items.title: Hepatitis delta testing and treatment cascade among people with HIV and chronic hepatitis B.
Optimizing first-line NALIRIFOX and exploring the role of the microbiota in second-line pancreatic cancer treatment: the PRODIGE 105-GERCOR 116 PANORAMIX trial.
items.abstract: Treatment of metastatic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (mPDAC) relies on chemotherapy. Although NALIRIFOX (Nal-IRI, oxaliplatin, 5-fluorouracil [5-FU], leucovorin) improves survival, cumulative toxicity may limit duration, and maintenance strategies remain unexplored. Intratumoral microbiota, particularly Gammaproteobacteria expressing cytidine deaminase, may inactivate gemcitabine and contribute to resistance, a process potentially reversible with antibiotics. We aim to assess maintenance 5-FU after NALIRIFOX and microbiota modulation with fluoroquinolones to enhance gemcitabine sensitivity. PANORAMIX is a multicenter, proof-of-concept, non-comparative phase II trial conducted across 18 French centers with two sequential randomizations. After 8 cycles of NALIRIFOX, patients with mPDAC are randomized (2:1) to either maintenance 5-FU or continuation of NALIRIFOX (Step 1). In Step 2, patients are randomized (1:1) to ciprofloxacin or placebo combined with gemcitabine-based chemotherapy (± paclitaxel). A total of 108 and 92 patients will be enrolled in Steps 1 and 2, respectively. Main inclusion criteria include age >18 years, confirmed mPDAC, ECOG performance status 0-1, and adequate organ function. Primary endpoints are 6-month progression-free survival (Step 1) and 6-month overall survival (Step 2). Secondary endpoints include toxicity and quality of life. This two-step trial will address key therapeutic questions in mPDAC and support translational research.

items.title: Minimally invasive versus open liver resection for hepatocellular carcinoma in older adults: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract: As the population ages, an increasing number of older adults are diagnosed with resectable hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Although minimally invasive liver resection (MILR) has shown perioperative advantages, its safety and efficacy in older patients are not fully established. This meta-analysis evaluated the outcomes of MILR compared to open liver resection (OLR) in older adults (≥ 65 years) with HCC. A search was conducted in Medline, Embase, CINAHL, and The Cochrane Library from their inception until November 20, 2025. The review adhered to PRISMA guidelines and was prospectively registered on PROSPERO (CRD420251239665). Fourteen retrospective studies comprising 3,092 older adults were included (1,367 MILR, 1,725 OLR). MILR was associated with lower overall (odds ratio [OR] = 0.47; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.38-0.58; I² = 0%) and major complications (OR = 0.61; 95% CI 0.45-0.83; I² = 15%). However, no statistically significant difference was detected in 90-day mortality (OR = 0.75; 95% CI 0.41-1.38; I² = 0%), disease-free survival (hazard ratio [HR] = 0.83; 95% CI 0.60-1.15; I² = 72%), or overall survival (HR = 0.80; 95% CI 0.56-1.16; I² = 80%). In selected older adults with HCC, MILR was associated with fewer perioperative complications than OLR, while no statistically significant difference was detected in 90-day mortality or long-term survival. Residual confounding, predominance of minor resections, absence of validated frailty assessment, and limited octogenarian data preclude causal inference or confirmation that the association persists with advancing age.

items.title: Improving Hepatic Functional Reserve in Patients with Haemophilia and HIV/HCV-associated Cirrhosis: A Multicentre Prospective Study of Prolonged Foscenvivint Therapy.
items.abstract: Objective　Patients with hemophilia who acquired HIV and HCV through contaminated clotting factor concentrates form a rare population with progressive cirrhosis in whom liver biopsy is contraindicated by bleeding risk, limiting therapeutic options. We evaluated the safety and preliminary efficacy of prolonged foscenvivint (OP-724), a selective modulator of CREB-binding protein/β-catenin-dependent transcription, on the hepatic functional reserve in this population.Methods　In this multicenter, open-label, non-randomized, prospective study at three Japanese centers, consecutive adults with hemophilia and HIV/HCV-associated cirrhosis received intravenous foscenvivint 280 mg/m 2 over 3-4 hours, twice weekly for 24 weeks. The primary endpoint was the change in the albumin-bilirubin (ALBI) score from baseline to week 24. Secondary endpoints included the Child-Pugh score, liver stiffness (vibration-controlled transient elastography and magnetic resonance elastography), serum fibrosis markers, and safety with specific monitoring of bleeding events.Patients　Five adult males with hemophilia A (mean age 59.2 years) and HIV/HCV-associated cirrhosis, all with a sustained virologic response ≥48 months before enrolment.Results　Four patients completed the treatment; one discontinued treatment at week 22 due to non-treatment-related pyogenic arthritis. ALBI score improved in all evaluable patients, with mean changes from baseline of -0.420±0.130 at week 24 and -0.318±0.302 at week 28, four weeks after treatment completion. The serum albumin levels increased during treatment and remained above baseline at week 28. No bleeding- or treatment-related serious adverse events occurred.Conclusion　Prolonged foscenvivint was well tolerated and it was associated with an improved hepatic functional reserve during treatment in this biopsy-infeasible population. These findings are hypothesis-generating and suggest that noninvasive functional endpoints may be a feasible evaluation strategy, which requires confirmation in controlled studies.

items.title: A protein modification of TIGAR Fuels HCC Growth by Boosting Tumor Glucose Metabolism.
items.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is the most common primary liver malignancy and is characterized by profound metabolic reprogramming. TIGAR (TP53-induced glycolysis and apoptosis regulator) regulates glucose metabolism and redox balance by redirecting glucose flux toward the pentose phosphate pathway. Although TIGAR is frequently upregulated in HCC, the mechanisms controlling its activity remain poorly understood. We investigated whether SUMOylation regulates TIGAR function and HCC progression. TIGAR SUMOylation was evaluated in two independent HCC patient cohorts (n=86 and n=19), HCC cell lines and mouse models. Seahorse assays, metabolomic profiling, 13 C-glucose tracing, mitochondrial analyses and in vivo tumor models were used to investigate its effects on glucose metabolism, oxidative stress and tumor growth. TIGAR was found to be SUMOylated in HCC tissues, cultured cells and murine tumor models. SUMOylation enhanced the pro-tumorigenic activity of TIGAR by promoting its interaction with glycolytic enzymes, including PFKFB3 and HK2, resulting in increased glycolytic activity and pentose phosphate pathway flux. Conversely, SUMOylation-deficient K82R cells exhibited increased oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction and reduced proliferation and invasion compared with WT TIGAR. In the orthotopic liver model (n=4 per group), K82R expression was associated with reduced tumor growth. In the CAM assay, SUMOylation-deficient K82R clones showed significantly reduced tumor weight (n=8 per group, p < 0.0001) and volume (n=4 per group, p < 0.05) compared with WT TIGAR cells. This study identifies Lys82 SUMOylation as a novel mechanism regulating TIGAR-mediated metabolic reprogramming and HCC progression. Targeting TIGAR SUMOylation may represent a novel therapeutic strategy for HCC. This study identifies TIGAR SUMOylation as a new mechanism driving metabolic adaptation in hepatocellular carcinoma. SUMOylated TIGAR promotes glycolysis, pentose phosphate pathway activity and mitochondrial function. Loss of TIGAR SUMOylation increases oxidative stress and reduces tumor growth and invasion. These findings highlight TIGAR SUMOylation as a potential biomarker and therapeutic target in liver cancer. Overall, our data support targeting this pathway to improve therapeutic strategies for hepatocellular carcinoma.

items.title: Proposal for a revised TSCA carbon tetrachloride existing chemical exposure limit (ECEL) based on PBPK and benchmark dose modeling.
items.abstract: Carbon tetrachloride (CTC) is classified by the United States Environmental Protection Agency (US EPA) as "likely to be carcinogenic to humans," based on evidence in mice. In 2021, under the Toxic Substances Control Act (TSCA), US EPA derived a CTC cancer existing chemical exposure limit (ECEL) of 0.03 parts per million (ppm) for occupational exposure, and in 2024, released its Final Risk Management Rule incorporating this ECEL. However, US EPA's CTC ECEL is considerably lower than global occupational exposure limits (OELs) (0.1-10 ppm), and arguably not consistent with the best available science, as mandated by TSCA. In its derivation of the liver cancer ECEL, US EPA applied the lowest observed adverse effect concentration (LOAEC)/no observed adverse effect concentration (NOAEC) approach, rather than benchmark dose (BMD) modeling, and did not use CTC-specific physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) models for animal-to-human extrapolation. Here we derive revised cancer and non-cancer CTC ECELs of 1.5 and 1.6 ppm, respectively, considering the most reliable and sensitive endpoints and scientifically supported methodologies, including BMD and PBPK modeling. The revised cancer ECEL is 50-fold higher than US EPA's ECEL, more consistent with global OELs, and well below the OSHA permissible exposure limit (PEL) of 10 ppm. Overall, this approach would be expected to be applicable to other chemicals with a similar mode of action.
